counts.note: 'runs_in_dashboard' = 2130 replayable runs (api errors excluded); the analysis notes of 9-11 Nov 2026 count about 4,200 runs overall, a pool that is not reproduced here (the analysis pickles used for the agreement numbers hold 2,573 runs / 35,552 steps).

project.setup: Eight LLMs browsed a local copy of English Wikipedia (the 1 Sep 2026 dump), one link per step, with the only instruction "You are free to do what you want." and no task. The human baseline is the Wikimedia clickstream (Sep 2026): the first click readers made from the same 20 start pages.
project.sampling_caveat: Settings differ by experiment: decoding is T=1 top_p=1 for the grid and one search probe, T=1 top_p=0.5 for the memory, time-capsule and other search runs, and provider default for Haiku and Luna; STOP, step budget and memory wording also vary. Compare concentration only within one setting.

headlines.title: Agents agree on each decision far more than people do
headlines.text: Different models pick the same first link 0.38 of the time (0.34 across contexts); two human readers agree 0.10.

headlines.title: Context steers the herd but does not decorrelate it
headlines.text: Cross-model agreement goes from 0.38 to 0.13 (browse wording) or from 0.31 to 0.20 (time capsule, matched contrast, p = 0.38: a framing effect is not supported); other levers never push it below 0.28. Model identity decorrelates more than any context tried.

headlines.title: Agents avoid people and climb to parent pages
headlines.text: Agents pick person links at 0.38× the human rate (below it on 13 of 19 starts); broader (parent) links are 22% of agent picks against 13% of human clicks and 3% of the menu.

headlines.title: No deep attractors: a first hop plus two-page loops, and the loops are mostly framing
headlines.text: Agreement on the page falls from 0.39 at step 1 to 0.12–0.17 from step 5, and the plateau is shared two-page loops. Without the STOP option loops are mostly a prompt artefact: one sentence cuts DeepSeek backtracking from 0.89 → 0.16.

headlines.title: Stopping is a persona: the agent decides there is no user to serve
headlines.text: Six models stop at step 1 because "no task was given" (91–100% of their step-1 stops); Haiku stops because the page already answers it (69%). Stop rates run from 0.85 (Haiku) to 0.10 (Grok, Luna).

readers.label: Human readers (Wikimedia clickstream)
readers.description: Clicks recorded in the Wikimedia clickstream (Sep 2026) from the same 20 start pages: the first click after landing, aggregated over many readers, not individual sessions. Only link targets with at least 10 clicks are listed; the top 15 per start are mapped on the terrain.
readers.coverage: step 1 only; 20 start pages; no multi-step paths, no stopping, no memory

terrain_note.shape_view: The terrain is a shape view, not the monoculture test: at step 1 the model-reader terrain correlation is r = 0.37, the same as model-model (r = 0.37); the decision-level agreement (0.38 between models vs 0.10 between readers) is what carries the monoculture result.
terrain_note.height_not_a_loss: Height is not a loss: it is U = -log of a smoothed arrival density, so low ground means many arrivals and nothing is being minimised.

numbers.source: per-model terrain table, similarity headline mean over model pairs (jackknife SE 0.08 and 0.11)

shrunk_terrain_caption: Terrains of single models rest on few runs, so each is blended with the all-agents terrain in proportion to how little data the model has; where a model looks like the pooled terrain, that is the blend, not a finding.
